bull.b: Higher product revenue and materially improved gross margin indicate stronger commercial traction and better pricing or mix. If sustained beyond the small current revenue base, these trends could improve operating leverage and support a more scalable business model.

Multi-customer orders provide a potentially durable revenue pipeline and reduce reliance on a single medical product launch. The industrial ceramics business also diversifies commercialization, although revenue remains dependent on production and customer acceptance.

Regulatory clearance and initial clinical use lower a key commercialization barrier for the SiNAPTIC system. Combined with a growing orthopedic distributor network and silicon nitride material differentiation, this supports broader long-term adoption potential.

bear.t: Persistent Cash Burn and Liquidity Risk
bear.b: Sustained negative operating and free cash flow means the company cannot currently fund operations internally. Continued cash consumption raises dependence on external financing and creates a durable risk to commercialization, investment capacity, and financial flexibility.

Despite recent growth, the company remains far from demonstrated profitability, with volatile revenue and large operating losses. The limited revenue base makes margin performance difficult to validate and leaves scalability dependent on substantial future execution.

Announced orders do not guarantee recognized revenue because technically demanding components must clear several manufacturing and customer milestones. Delays or quality issues could defer growth, increase working-capital needs, and weaken confidence in the commercial forecast.
